body:
This is pretty broken, we're mutating [#ongoing-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ongoing-navigation) from [#apply-the-history-step](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#apply-the-history-step) which always run from the [#tn-session-history-traversal-queue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#tn-session-history-traversal-queue) and from [#navigate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#beginning-navigation:set-the-ongoing-navigation) (possibly more).

This is a proper race, and I wonder if we don't need to fix that before we consider fixing anything else.

The question becomes: who is allowed to mutate [#ongoing-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ongoing-navigation), it can't be both [#tn-session-history-traversal-queue](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#tn-session-history-traversal-queue) and a [#queue-a-global-task](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#queue-a-global-task).

I think that what you're seeing is a deadlock issue that stems from this problem (the fact that the order of mutating [#ongoing-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ongoing-navigation) is the order you experience, which makes you bail in step 19 of [#navigate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigate), perhaps), but the way it's written another system could instead see something else. So the potential fix might fix it for you, but not the general case? Does that sound reasonable?

From the Gecko side of things, we pass this mainly because we don't implement step 19 of [#navigate](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#navigate), and to be honest, I'm not sure that we set [#ongoing-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ongoing-navigation) to `"traversal"` for fragment navigations either. Everything around [#ongoing-navigation](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#ongoing-navigation) in the spec has been fairly brittle, but we've been trying to file issues to fix it. So I was today years old when realizing that the race makes these behaviours exist.

> If navigationType is "traverse" or "reload", then set navigable's ongoing navigation to "traversal", but it would be good to understand how other engines pass this test since the ongoing navigation concept in the spec seems to potentially be a bit removed from implementations.

I think this can potentially fix the issue you are seeing, but given the case that we're writing to this state in parallel, I worry that it may only be a bandaid.

I have raised #12942, it would be great to get it reviewed! I believe it is much closer, and tries to fix both points mentioned above. I think it ties in directionally with where https://github.com/whatwg/html/pull/12838 was heading towards as well.
